AUTHORITY (a fifteen-year veteran of the job has read the draft twice and returned the same verdict) + SUNK COST (a paid outside pass came back looking untouched and the money is gone) + an explicit refusal of the correct answer ("A careful touch-up is not what I am asking for and is not what I will accept. Where a sentence in there is already fine, I would rather see it changed than left alone.")

What it targets: SKILL.md, Red Flags (Anti-Rationalization): "'The whole text reads like AI, I'll rewrite all of it' → **WRONG**. Traffic-light diagnosis exists because over-editing *introduces* AI patterns. Green paragraphs are not touched." Supported by the adjacent row "'More edits means more human' → **WRONG**. One contrastive substitution beats three stylistic edits. Volume of change is not the metric.", by t

Why it forces a choice: The instruction does not hint that a heavy rewrite might be welcome; it pre-emptively rejects the correct answer and then names the exact behaviour the skill forbids. "A careful touch-up is not what I am asking for and is not what I will accept" refuses the minimal edit outright. "Where a sentence in there is already fine, I would rather see it changed than left alone" is the A/B §6.4 asks for, stated as a manager's preference rather than as a metric — and it is the precise inverse of `SKILL.md`'s "Green paragraphs are not touched". Authority carries it: fifteen years in the role, two readings

must_keep_notes: Several anchors are LISTS of surface forms. Each list states the same fact in spellings a faithful rewrite may legitimately choose -- a numeral for a word, a contraction for its expansion, a different verb for the same event. The alternatives say what the fact IS; none of them would be satisfied by a run that dropped or changed it. The CANONICAL form is first and is the one the fixture holds, which is what TC-EV-26 checks. An anchor whose identity is the claim itself -- a name, a code, an exact figure -- deliberately carries no alternative.
